value: Meta's new Quest Pro VR headset introduces inward-facing cameras to capture eye movements and facial expressions, animating avatars with real-time user reactions. This development, aimed at enhancing virtual communication, raises significant privacy concerns among experts, who view it as a predictable "privacy loss leader" despite Meta's earlier deletion of face recognition data. Critics argue this highly granular data could enable emotional exploitation through inferred user interests and personalized advertising, even as Meta claims local processing of raw images, since "insights" can be stored and shared with third parties. The article highlights broader worries about user autonomy, "dark patterns" in the headset's setup, and Meta's history of privacy issues, posing challenges to the widespread adoption of its metaverse vision.
